unit.title: Learning to read Russian
unit.topicSummary: Content-complete development unit for printed letters: identities, print pairs, look-alikes, signs, and letter-level decoding. Qualified review and the owned-edition mapping are still pending.
unit.mappingNote: Proposed Lesson 1 mapping from the publisher's public table of contents. Owned-edition comparison is not signed, so this unit is not labeled aligned.

objectives.title: Separate Cyrillic letters from Latin look-alikes
Recognize Е Ё Ю Я as a group
Treat Ь Ъ Й as non-ordinary-vowel letters
Match uppercase and lowercase print pairs
Confirm letter sounds in the book
Treat stress as book-marked, not guessed
Complete Lesson 1 work in the owned book

steps.title: Unit 1 — Printed letters
steps.body: This is a proposed Lesson 1 mapping, not an approved owned-edition alignment. The development unit teaches printed letter identities with public-domain letter forms. Example words and model audio are not part of this unit. Qualified review is still pending.
steps.bookDirection: Open your copy to Lesson 1. Use the book for the author's explanations, exercises, and any example words.

steps.title: Identify letters first
steps.body: Work letter shapes, print pairs, and Latin look-alikes before later reading. Transliteration, if you use it, is a temporary support.

steps.title: Cyrillic is a different alphabet
steps.body: Russian is written with 33 Cyrillic letters. Some printed shapes look like Latin letters and are not the same letters. Learn identity first.

steps.title: First vowel set
steps.body: Work these printed pairs: А а, О о, У у, Э э, Ы ы, И и. English sound notes are pending qualified review.

steps.title: Identify А
steps.body: Choose the Cyrillic identity for the printed letter.

steps.title: Low-confusion consonants
steps.body: Next printed pairs: М м, Т т, К к, П п, Б б, Д д, Г г. Confirm each spoken sound in your book. This unit does not play model audio.

steps.title: Identify М
steps.body: Choose the Cyrillic identity for the printed letter.

steps.title: Shape traps
steps.body: These printed letters often fool Latin-alphabet readers: В, Н, Р, С, У, Х. Name the Cyrillic identity. Read this as a review-pending explanation. Worked examples come before the guided choice, and the independent check is separate. A wrong answer returns to this contrast. Activity is not demonstrated ability.

steps.title: Guided contrast
steps.body: These printed letters often fool Latin-alphabet readers: В, Н, Р, С, У, Х. Name the Cyrillic identity. Choose once with the explanation still in view. This is practice, not the independent check.

steps.title: Р is not P
steps.body: Identity check.

steps.title: Н is not H
steps.body: Identity check.

steps.title: С is not C
steps.body: Identity check.

steps.title: В, У, and Х
steps.body: Identity check for the remaining look-alikes.

steps.title: Е Ё Ю Я
steps.body: Recognize these printed forms as a group. Exact phonetics belong in your book. Read this as a review-pending explanation. Worked examples come before the guided choice, and the independent check is separate. A wrong answer returns to this contrast. Activity is not demonstrated ability.

steps.title: Guided contrast
steps.body: Recognize these printed forms as a group. Exact phonetics belong in your book. Choose once with the explanation still in view. This is practice, not the independent check.

steps.title: Identify Е, Ё, Ю, and Я
steps.body: Identity check.

sessions.title: Soft sign, hard sign, and Й

steps.title: Marks that are not ordinary vowels
steps.body: Ь, Ъ, and Й need special attention. Do not invent a spoken vowel for the signs. Read this as a review-pending explanation. Worked examples come before the guided choice, and the independent check is separate. A wrong answer returns to this contrast. Activity is not demonstrated ability.

steps.title: Guided contrast
steps.body: Ь, Ъ, and Й need special attention. Do not invent a spoken vowel for the signs. Choose once with the explanation still in view. This is practice, not the independent check.

steps.title: Soft sign
steps.body: Identity check.

steps.title: Hard sign
steps.body: Identity check.

steps.title: Й is not a vowel
steps.body: Identity check.

steps.title: Uppercase and lowercase together
steps.body: Every letter has a print pair. Match them on the letter board. Handwritten forms wait for verified assets.

steps.title: Guided contrast
steps.body: Every letter has a print pair. Match them on the letter board. Handwritten forms wait for verified assets. Choose once with the explanation still in view. This is practice, not the independent check.

steps.title: Match a print pair
steps.body: Identity check.

steps.title: Decode print pairs
steps.body: Name the letter, then match its uppercase and lowercase print forms. This unit does not introduce words.
steps.bookDirection: Use the elementary reading work in your Lesson 1 pages for anything beyond a single letter.

steps.title: Guided contrast
steps.body: Name the letter, then match its uppercase and lowercase print forms. This unit does not introduce words. Choose once with the explanation still in view. This is practice, not the independent check.
steps.bookDirection: Use the elementary reading work in your Lesson 1 pages for anything beyond a single letter.

steps.title: One letter, two cases
steps.body: Choose the line that is a single letter.

steps.title: Confirm sounds in your book
steps.body: This unit does not play model audio. Use the pronunciation notes in your book for each new letter. A recording you make is stored and is not scored.
steps.bookDirection: Read the Lesson 1 pronunciation notes in the edition you own.

steps.title: Stress is part of reading
steps.body: Russian word stress is not predictable from spelling alone. Marked example words are not installed.
steps.bookDirection: When your Lesson 1 pages mark stress, copy that mark into your binder.

steps.body: Complete the Lesson 1 reading and pronunciation work in the edition you own.

steps.bookDirection: Use your Lesson 1 pages for the author's pronunciation notes. This list is the app's name inventory.

steps.title: Guided letter name
steps.body: The printed letter А is named а. Choose that name before the independent check.

steps.title: Letter-name remediation
steps.body: Return to the printed name. А is named а. Б is named бэ. Do not use the Latin letter name.

steps.title: Letter-name check
steps.body: Name the printed letter without looking back at the list.

items.prompt: Which printed letter is shown?
items.feedback: The printed shape can match Latin A. In this course it is the Cyrillic vowel letter А.

items.prompt: Which printed letter is shown?
items.feedback: М is an early consonant letter. It is not Н.

items.prompt: This letter looks like Latin P. What is it?
items.feedback: Shape overlap with Latin P is a recognition trap. This is Cyrillic Р, not English P.

items.prompt: This letter looks like Latin H. What is it?
items.feedback: Do not read Н as English H. It is a Cyrillic letter.

items.prompt: This letter looks like Latin C. What is it?
items.feedback: С is a Cyrillic letter. Do not treat the Latin look-alike as the identity.

items.prompt: This letter looks like Latin B. What is it?
items.feedback: В is not Latin B and it is not Cyrillic Б.

items.prompt: This letter looks like Latin Y. What is it?
items.feedback: У is a Cyrillic vowel letter, not Latin Y.

items.prompt: This letter looks like Latin X. What is it?
items.feedback: Х is a Cyrillic letter, not Latin X.

items.prompt: Which printed letter is shown?
items.feedback: Ё is its own letter. Е and Э are different letters.

items.prompt: Which printed letter is shown?
items.feedback: Ю is an iotated vowel letter. У and Я are different letters.

items.prompt: Which printed letter is shown?
items.feedback: Я is an iotated vowel letter. It is not Р or А.

items.prompt: What is the printed letter Й?
options: A consonant letter, not a vowel
items.answer: A consonant letter, not a vowel
items.feedback: Й is not a vowel you read alone and it is not the soft sign.

items.prompt: Which line is one letter written in both print cases?
items.feedback: А / а is one letter. The other lines are two different letters.

items.prompt: Which printed letter is shown?
items.feedback: Е is an iotated vowel letter. Э and Ё are different letters.

items.prompt: What is the printed mark Ь?
options: A vowel you pronounce by itself
A mark, not a standalone vowel
items.answer: A mark, not a standalone vowel
items.feedback: Ь is a sign, not a vowel letter you read alone.

items.prompt: What is the printed mark Ъ?
options: The hard sign, not a vowel
items.answer: The hard sign, not a vowel
items.feedback: Ъ is the hard sign. It is not a spoken vowel and it is not Ь.

items.prompt: Which pair is the same letter in uppercase and lowercase print?
items.feedback: Print pairs are one letter in two cases. Р / п and Н / и are different letters.

items.prompt: Which name belongs to this printed letter?
items.feedback: The printed letter А is named а.

items.prompt: Which name belongs to this printed letter?
items.feedback: The printed letter Б is named бэ.

items.prompt: The shape looks like Latin P. Which identity is the Cyrillic letter?
items.feedback: Р is the Cyrillic letter, even when the shape looks like Latin P.

items.prompt: Which printed form is the iotated letter named in this group?
items.feedback: Я belongs to the iotated group. Exact phonetics stay with the book model you own.

items.prompt: What does this sign do?
options: It marks softness and is not a vowel
It is the Latin letter b
items.answer: It marks softness and is not a vowel
items.feedback: Ь and Ъ are signs. Do not invent a spoken vowel for them.

items.prompt: Which lowercase print form pairs with this uppercase letter?
items.feedback: Match the printed uppercase and lowercase pair. Handwriting assets are not installed.

items.prompt: Read the printed pair before any word. Which lowercase form matches?
items.feedback: Decode the print pair first. This guided step still does not score a whole word.
